title: Riverside footbridge: repair or replace?
question: Should the council repair the Riverside footbridge, replace it, or replace it with a wider bridge for walking and cycling?
summary: A 1974 steel footbridge is corroding. It is the only step-free crossing to a school and a row of shops. This map shows the options, what a closure would be like for the people who use the bridge, and what the council still has to decide. All names and figures are made up.

checked.note: Checked against the principal inspection, early cost estimates and one public drop-in session.

glossary.load rating: The weight a bridge can safely carry, worked out by an engineer.
glossary.bearings: The parts at each end that let the bridge move a little as it warms and cools.
glossary.section loss: Steel lost to rust, as a share of the original thickness.
glossary.shared use: A path for people walking and cycling together.

roles.label: Safety
roles.asks: How do we keep people safe before, during and after the work?

roles.asks: What does this mean for the people who cross every day?

roles.label: Finance
roles.asks: What does each option cost over its whole life, and who pays?

evidence.text: Corrosion at 6 of 14 lower joints; two show section loss over 20%.
With repairs, another 25 years is realistic. Without them, we would recommend a weight limit within three years.
Bearings at the north end have seized; the bridge cannot expand freely in summer.
Repair £1.1m, 10 weeks closed, 25 years. Replace £3.4m, 9 months closed, 100 years. Wider replacement £4.2m, 11 months, 100 years.
A regional cycling fund could pay up to 40% of a widened bridge, if bid by November.
The river authority needs 6 months' notice for any work in the water.
It's the only step-free way to the school. A long closure means a 20-minute walk round by the main road.
It's too narrow to pass anyone. If you're rebuilding, make it wider.
Last time it shut for a month, my takings dropped by a third.
The ramps at the north end are too steep for me on my own.

gaps.title: A way across during a long closure
gaps.why: A nine-month closure without a crossing cuts off the school's only step-free route.

stories.as: As a parent with a pram, I want a step-free way across while the bridge is shut, so the school run stays under ten minutes.
done_when: a temporary crossing or shuttle runs at school times
the route is signed and lit
the detour is no more than 10 minutes longer

gaps.title: Ramps people can use on their own
gaps.why: The north ramps are too steep for some wheelchair users.

stories.as: As a wheelchair user, I want ramps I can manage alone, so I do not need help to cross.
done_when: ramp slopes meet the access standard
a wheelchair user tests the design before it is approved

the bid shows the drop-in feedback

notes.title: Repairs buy 25 years, not 100
notes.body: Repair is sound engineering, but the bridge will need replacing in the 2050s anyway.
notes.recommend: Compare options over 50 years, not on build cost alone.
notes.question: Do we judge the options over 50 years of cost and closures?

notes.title: The river notice sets the earliest start
notes.body: Any option needs six months' notice for work in the water.
notes.recommend: Send a notice for the larger option now; it can be narrowed later.
notes.question: Can we give notice before the committee decides?

notes.title: Seized bearings are a summer risk
notes.body: A bridge that cannot expand is stressed on hot days.
notes.recommend: Free or replace the north bearings this year, whatever we decide.
notes.question: Do we fix the bearings now as urgent work?

notes.title: The school run is the hardest hit
notes.body: Families with prams have no other step-free route.
notes.recommend: Plan the closure around school holidays where possible.
notes.question: Can the longest part of the works fall in the summer holidays?

notes.title: Shops felt the last closure
notes.body: One owner lost a third of takings during a one-month closure.
notes.recommend: Talk to the south-side shops before setting dates; consider signs that say 'shops open'.
notes.question: Is there any support we can offer shops during a long closure?

notes.title: Fix the ramps in either option
notes.body: A repair could rebuild the north ramps too.
notes.recommend: Include gentler ramps in the repair option so the comparison is fair.
notes.question: Does the repair price include new ramps?

notes.title: The fund changes the sums
notes.body: With 40% from the fund, the wider bridge costs the council about £2.5m.
notes.recommend: Show the committee both prices: with and without the fund.
notes.question: Do we commit to the wider option if the bid fails?

notes.title: The estimates are rough
notes.body: At ±30%, repair and replace overlap less than they seem, but the ranking could still shift.
notes.question: Do we wait for firmer prices before deciding?

notes.title: Say what we are aiming for
notes.body: Residents care about the closure as much as the bridge.
notes.recommend: State the aim as a safe crossing with the shortest closure we can manage.
notes.question: Which matters more to the committee: lowest cost or shortest closure?

notes.title: An assistant can draft the weekly update
notes.body: Site photos and the contractor's diary hold most of the news.
notes.recommend: Let an assistant draft the Friday update from the diary; a council officer approves it.
notes.question: Who approves the weekly update before it goes out?

notes.title: Wider means safer, not just nicer
notes.body: People cannot pass on the current width.
notes.recommend: Treat 4 m as the access option, not an extra.
notes.question: Is 4 m enough for the expected number of cycles?

decisions.question: Do we fix the seized bearings now?
options: No, wait for the main decision
decisions.decision: Yes. Bearings freed in August as urgent works.

decisions.question: How do people cross during a long closure?

outcomes.target: As few as the chosen option allows
